source: Canadian National Autism Foundation, cnaf.net/provinceres.html; each entry checked on its own website

entries.name: Early Childhood Development Association of PEI (ECDA)
entries.description: A provincial non-profit association, formed in 1974, that promotes quality early learning and child care on Prince Edward Island and supports the early childhood education workforce with resources and professional learning. For families, it points to the PEI Early Learning and Child Care Registry, a tool for searching and signing up for regulated child care programs.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost for families.
entries.evidence: The PEI ELCC Registry provides families with a powerful tool to search and sign-up for regulated early learning and child care programs across PEI.
entries.notes: CNAF links to http://earlychildhooddevelopment.ca/; that now redirects to the association's current site, https://ecdaofpei.ca/. The association mainly serves early childhood educators (membership, careers, training) and says it champions healthy development for PEI children aged 0 to 12. Phone is from the Contact page; the email there is hidden by an email-protection script, so it is left out.

entries.name: Autism Society of PEI
entries.description: A provincial charity that supports autistic Islanders and their families from before diagnosis onward, with social programming, parent and caregiver supports, education and training resources, help navigating services, and advocacy resources. Newly diagnosed families can arrange a meeting to get a Family Diagnosis Package that explains provincial and federal autism services.
entries.cost_note: Family membership is $50 per year and gives access to family events, parent training, diagnosis kits, the autism library and subsidized programming.
entries.address: 161 St. Peters Road, Sherwood Business Centre Charlottetown, PE
entries.evidence: The Autism Society of PEI strives to enhance the lives of Autistic Islanders and their families.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added under step 4 because CNAF's PEI page yields only one other entry. Toll-free 1-888-360-8681. The site lists only named staff email addresses, so email is left blank. Registered charity #139029301 RR 0001; member of the Autism Alliance of Canada.

entries.name: Prince Edward Island Association for Community Living (PEIACL)
entries.description: A province-wide, family-based association for Islanders with intellectual disabilities and their families, and a member of Inclusion Canada. Its Supporting Families program gives information and referrals, support and advocacy at school, AccessAbility and other planning meetings, parent support networks and parent-to-parent connections, and help planning the move to life after high school.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: Guided by the needs of each individual, we provide support and advocacy services in various environments, such as schools, government offices, places of employment, and family homes.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because PEI has only 2 checked services. Supporting Families asks for at least a self-identified diagnosis and also supports parents, guardians and siblings; PEIACL's Ready, Willing and Able program connects people with an intellectual disability or ASD with employers. Address (Royalty Centre, Charlottetown) and phone are from the Contact page; the site's email address is hidden by an email-protection script.

entries.name: Learning Disabilities Association of PEI (LDAPEI)
entries.description: A registered charity that supports Islanders with learning disabilities, including people with suspected learning disabilities, and their families. It offers one-on-one tutoring in reading (the Barton program, in person or online), math and other subjects, executive functioning programs, monthly parent support groups in Charlottetown and Summerside, workshops, and information and referrals.
entries.cost_note: Reading tutoring is a registration fee plus $45 per session; the Executive Functioning seminar-workshop series is free.
entries.evidence: LDAPEI staff are available to meet and speak with children, parents and adults regarding learning disabilities.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because PEI has only 2 checked services. Second office at 30 Greenwood Drive, Suite 18, Summerside. New clients start with the contact form; in-person tutoring is at hub sites (a school, a community location or the LDAPEI office), not in homes. Phone, email and addresses are from the Contact page.

entries.name: Camp Gencheff
entries.description: A non-profit in Stratford with year-round programs for children, youth and adults with intellectual and physical disabilities: an adult day program, an after-school program, a children's summer day camp, PD-day and school-break camps, and overnight weekend respite two to three times a month.
entries.cost_note: The after-school program is $20.00 per day and PD-day camp is $75; the adult day program is priced on the client's needs.
entries.evidence: Camp Gencheff offers a variety of year-round programs for adults and children with intellectual and physical disabilities.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because PEI has only 2 checked services. To join, families contact the camp, fill in an application and have a 'Meet & Greet' with intake staff. Contact details are from the site footer; charitable number 105201065 RR 0001.

entries.name: Accessibility Services (University of Prince Edward Island)
entries.description: UPEI's office for students with documented visible or invisible, temporary or permanent disabilities, including learning and mental health disabilities; it also supports neurodiverse students. Registered students can get accommodations for classroom learning and test taking.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention a cost for the service.
entries.evidence: UPEI Accessibility Services supports students with documented visible or invisible, temporary or permanent disabilities.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because PEI has only 2 checked services. The office is in Robertson Library (Monday to Friday, 8:00 am to 12:00 pm and 1:00 to 4:00 pm); students register through Symplicity Accommodate and may have to upload medical documentation. Holland College's supports are already in colleges_ca.json; this is the university's office.

entries.name: ResourceAbilities
entries.description: PEI's cross-disability organization, formerly the PEI Council of People with Disabilities, with offices in Charlottetown, Summerside and Montague. Its Community Access Workers help Islanders with disabilities apply for and navigate programs such as AccessAbility Supports, Income Support, the Disability Tax Credit, CPP Disability and the RDSP, and advocate for them. It also runs employment services, a summer tutoring program for K-12 students with disabilities, a Snoezelen room and accessible parking permits.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention a cost for help with benefits; summer tutoring is $150 for the eight-week program.
entries.address: 5 Lower Malpeque Road, Unit #2, Landmark Plaza, Charlottetown
entries.evidence: Community Access Workers assist Islanders living with disabilities, and help navigate any provincial government system.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because PEI has only 2 checked services. The History page says it began in 1974 as the PEI Council of the Disabled, became the PEI Council of People with Disabilities in 2007 and approved the ResourceAbilities name after 2018 consultations; the old peicod.pe.ca domain no longer resolves. Contact details are the Queens County office; Summerside 902-436-9259, Montague 902-838-5878. The Contact page also lists an Autism Employment Program email, Autism@ResourceAbilities.ca.

entries.name: Employment Services and Counselling (ResourceAbilities)
entries.description: ResourceAbilities' employment program for job seekers with disabilities on PEI, run by Employment Specialists in its three county offices. It helps with career decisions, finding training and funding, job search skills such as resumes, cover letters and interviews, and keeping a job; its Abilities@Work program pays employers a wage subsidy, with job coaching, when they hire an eligible person with a disability.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention a cost for job seekers; the program is funded through the Canada-PEI Labour Market Agreements.
entries.evidence: The Employment Services and Counselling program is a comprehensive program that assists job seekers with disabilities.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because PEI has only 2 checked services; a separate program from the ResourceAbilities entry. County contacts: Queens 902-892-9149 ext. 231 or 233 (EmployQueens@ResourceAbilities.ca), Prince 902-436-9259 (Employment@ResourceAbilities.ca), Kings 902-838-5878. Abilities@Work participants must have a disability, be legally entitled to work in Canada and be ineligible for Employment Insurance assistance.

entries.name: Special Olympics PEI
entries.description: Sport for Islanders with an intellectual disability, with more than 100 weekly programs in communities across PEI. Community programs include Active Start for children aged 2 to 6, FUNdamentals for ages 7 to 12 and adult programs from age 13, and athletes 13 and older can also train and compete in competitive sport.
entries.cost_note: The site lists no fees and says no potential athlete is excluded because of financial constraint.
entries.evidence: Special Olympics PEI offers all Islanders with an intellectual disability access to sport.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because PEI has only 2 checked services. Athletes fill in an online Athlete Registration Form, then sign up for each season's programs (fall/winter sign-up opened 5 October 2026). Toll free 1-800-287-1196. The site is a section of specialolympics.ca.
